title: Implement three stage restricted allpass diffuser
description:
Create Source/DSP/ShortDiffuser.h and Source/DSP/ShortDiffuser.cpp implementing the restricted short diffusion stage for ShredSpace.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp (where the diffuser will later be called, after saturation and before the feedback tap)
- Any existing Source/DSP/*.h module and match its namespace, pragma-once/header-guard style, include style, and naming conventions exactly
- CMakeLists.txt (C++20 standard, JUCE modules available) but do not edit it

Required behavior (implement exactly these values and equations):
1. Exactly three cascaded first-order allpass stages per channel. No more, no fewer, and no additional reverb tail structure.
2. Transfer function per stage: H(z) = (-a + z^-M) / (1 - a*z^-M), realized by the difference equation y[n] = -a*x[n] + x[n-M] + a*y[n-M], where M is the stage delay in samples.
3. Stage delays: left channel 3.1 ms, 4.7 ms, 6.9 ms; right channel 3.7 ms, 5.3 ms, 7.9 ms. Coefficients a: 0.45, 0.38, 0.32 for stages one, two, three on both channels. Convert milliseconds to samples using the prepared sample rate and round to an integer sample count of at least 1.
4. User control d has range [0, 0.40]; the 0.40 cap applies to the normalized blend value before the equal-power law. Clamp d to [0, 0.40] on entry.
5. Equal-power blend: z_diff = cos(pi*d/2)*z + sin(pi*d/2)*allpass(z), where z is the dry input to the diffuser and allpass(z) is the three-stage cascade output.
6. Output must remain bounded (allpass stages have unity magnitude response; |a| < 1 guarantees stability). Introduce no independent late-reverb tail, no feedback across stages beyond the allpass recursions themselves, and no modulation of the stage delays.

API shape: a class ShortDiffuser with prepare(double sampleRate, int maxBlockSize), reset(), setAmount(float d), and per-channel processing (channel index 0 = left delays, 1 = right delays). Allocate all stage delay lines in prepare, sized for the longest stage at the highest supported sample rate (192 kHz); the process path must never resize a buffer. Smooth d with a linear juce::SmoothedValue at 30 ms (normalized control).

Real-time rules (binding): no heap allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, GUI calls, unbounded loops, or buffer resizing in the process path; all state allocated in prepare. reset() must clear all delay-line state to zero and leave no denormal residue.

Do not modify DelayVoice, CMakeLists.txt, or any other file; integration and build registration happen in task e.5. No artist or song names may appear anywhere in the source.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/ShortDiffuser.h and Source/DSP/ShortDiffuser.cpp exist and declare/define a ShortDiffuser class with prepare, reset, setAmount, and per-channel processing
ShortDiffuser.cpp implements exactly three first-order allpass stages per channel using y[n] = -a*x[n] + x[n-M] + a*y[n-M]
Stage delays are 3.1/4.7/6.9 ms on the left channel and 3.7/5.3/7.9 ms on the right channel, with coefficients 0.45/0.38/0.32
The user amount d is clamped to [0, 0.40] and blended with z_diff = cos(pi*d/2)*z + sin(pi*d/2)*allpass(z)
ShortDiffuser output stays bounded for bounded input and adds no independent late-reverb tail or extra feedback path
All delay-line storage is allocated in prepare sized for 192 kHz; no allocation, locking, file IO, or string construction occurs in process-path functions
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/ModulationEngine.h, Source/DSP/ModulationEngine.cpp, Source/DSP/SoftSaturator.h, Source/DSP/SoftSaturator.cpp, Source/DSP/StereoProcessor.h, or Source/DSP/StereoProcessor.cpp
add more than three allpass stages per channel
raise the diffusion amount cap above 0.40
add a late-reverb tail, extra feedback network, or delay-line modulation to the diffuser
allocate memory, lock, construct strings, or perform file IO inside process-path functions
include artist or song names in source or comments
